ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, through the centroid \(G\) of \(\triangle ABC\), construct \(ED\parallel AB\) meeting sides \(AC\) and \(BC\) at points \(E\) and \(D\) respectively. Connect \(AD\). If \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAC\) and \(AB=6\), what is the length of \(EC\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}:
Draw and extend CG to meet AB at H,\\
since G is the centroid of $\triangle ABC$\\
therefore $\frac{CG}{GH}=2$\\
therefore $\frac{CG}{CH}=\frac{2}{3}$\\
since $ED\parallel AB$\\
therefore $\frac{CG}{CH}=\frac{2}{3}=\frac{EC}{AC}$, $\angle ADE=\angle BAD$, $\triangle ECD\sim \triangle ACB$\\
therefore $\frac{EC}{AC}=\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{2}{3}$\\
therefore $DE=\frac{2}{3}AB=4$\\
since AD bisects $\angle BAC$\\
therefore $\angle EAD=\angle BAD$\\
therefore $\angle EAD=\angle ADE$\\
therefore $DE=AE=4$\\
therefore $\frac{2}{3}=\frac{EC}{AC}=\frac{EC}{EC+AE}$,\\
therefore $EC=\boxed{8}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, with A above and slightly to the left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and BC approximately horizontal. Point E is located on side AC, point D is located on side BC, and segment ED passes through the interior of the triangle and through the marked point G; AD is also connected in the figure. Combining with the problem statement, G is the centroid of triangle ABC, ED is parallel to AB, AD is the angle bisector of angle BAC, and AB=6. Then reason: Taking A as the origin, use vectors B and C to represent the position vectors of vertices B and C. Let |B|=AB=6 and |C|=AC=x. Because G is the centroid of triangle ABC, G=(B+C)/3. The line through G and parallel to AB has the same direction as B, so it can be written as G+sB=(B+C)/3+sB. Its intersection E with AC lies on AC, so E=tC. Thus tC=(B+C)/3+sB. Comparing the coefficients of B and C, in order for the coefficient of B to be 0, there is 1/3+s=0; the coefficient of C is t=1/3. Therefore AE=AC/3 and EC=2AC/3. By the angle bisector theorem, AD bisects angle BAC, so BD:DC=AB:AC=6:x. Point D lies on BC, and its vector can be written as D=(xB+6C)/(x+6). On the other hand, D also lies on the line through E and parallel to AB, so its C coefficient should be the same as the C coefficient of E, namely 1/3. Therefore 6/(x+6)=1/3, solving gives 18=x+6, x=12. Therefore AC=12, and EC=(2/3)AC=(2/3)·12=8.
